title: Fried Design Company's Award-Winning Ozarks Cryptid Skate Decks
excerpt: Josh Sullivan, owner and executive creative director of Fried Design Company, has loved skating since he was a kid. Now, he’s helping the next generation of skateboarders achieve their dreams by giving away his company’s award-winning Ozarks cryptid–themed skate decks in collaboration with the Springfield-Greene County Park Board.
content:
Lifestyle

Josh Sullivan, owner and executive creative director of Fried Design Company, has loved skating since he was a kid. Now, he’s helping the next generation of skateboarders achieve their dreams by giving away his company’s award-winning Ozarks cryptid–theme

Alyssa Roney

Nov 2026

When Josh Sullivan was a teenager, he had a favorite Springfield spot to kill time at: the Springfield Skate Park. At the time, the park was privately owned, and it offered a place for Sullivan to sharpen his skills.

Now Sullivan is the owner and executive creative director of Fried Design Company. After leaving and returning to Springfield, he made it a mission to provide not-for-profit work through his graphic design company as a way of giving back to Springfield. “The big thing for us is we don’t want to just give money,” Sullivan says. “If we can do something cool where we can give our art, that’s so much more interesting for us.”

Sullivan’s work came full circle when Fried Design Company partnered with the Springfield Skate Park by sponsoring skate camps. Over the years, they have produced T-shirts, stickers and skate decks (the flat part of a board) for the kids. For Sullivan, this means kids can come home with a keepsake that they might not have been able to purchase.


Creative Cryptids

Fried Design Company’s latest project for the skate park earned them recognition in not only the local sphere, but the national as well. Earlier in 2026, Fried Design Company took home a gold ADDY Award, a recognition given through the American Advertising Awards, for their work on skate decks for Springfield skate camps. This was followed by a gold award at the superregional level.

The project in question was a limited-edition skate deck series, with each deck featuring a different creature from Ozarks folklore. These include the Ozark Howler, a bear-sized shaggy beast with glowing red eyes and horns; Gowrow, a tusked, cave-dwelling reptile; and Momo, a Bigfoot-esque furry humanoid. The skate decks were the brainchild of Fried Design Company’s senior designer and illustrator, Tyler Crowe. Crowe, along with Sullivan and Bryan Elliott, associate creative director, treated the pro bono skate decks with care, setting aside nearly 45 hours total for each deck.

The character designs draw from the cultural well of skateboarding, something Sullivan is all too familiar with. He says that he enjoyed being pushed to experiment with illustration style and typography while working in an interesting canvas layout, with the intention of making the characters truly “rock ’n’ roll.”

After the team finishes their work, art files are sent to the Springfield Skate Park, which prints and sells them to raise money for seasonal skate camps and gives them away to young skateboarders.


Rolling Forward

Sullivan says he is excited to continue making an impact on kids through his company’s partnership with the Springfield-Greene County Park Board.

With another ADDY Award under Sullivan’s belt, the park board can be assured that Fried Design Company’s work is of the highest caliber.

“Whenever you see something that you’ve invested so much time and money in, and you’re able to share that win with them and give them a reaffirmation that they made a good decision in going with us, even though it was free, it was just a nice thing to have,” Sullivan says. “The awards are one thing, but being able to see how psyched the kids are to get this is even better.”
